<!-- https://kernlize.github.io/docs/packages/index.md -->

# Packages

kernl has four packages under the `@kernl` scope, not yet published to npm (see [Install](#install)). Three are pure contracts and engines with zero framework dependencies; one composes them with kehto and applesauce. The shell app at `apps/web` is not published.

| Package | Version | Role | Dependencies | Peer dependencies |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [`@kernl/guard`](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/packages/guard.md) | `0.1.0` | Ingress flood control, visibility gate, focus-aware firewall, CSP profile, nested-frame lock, mitigation descriptions. | `@kehto/firewall` | `@napplet/core` |
| [`@kernl/messaging`](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/packages/messaging.md) | `0.1.0` | Messaging provider contract, registry, composite direct-message adapter, in-memory backend. | none | `@napplet/core` (the `Dm*` wire types) |
| [`@kernl/bridges`](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/packages/bridges.md) | `0.1.0` | Locator parsing, bridge contract, registry, HTTP bridge with SSRF policy. | none | none |
| [`@kernl/core`](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/packages/core.md) | `0.1.0` | Composition root over kehto and applesauce: adapters, applet resolution, mount plan, consent summaries, layouts, persistence. | the three above, `@kehto/*`, `applesauce-*`, `rxjs` | `@napplet/core`, `@napplet/nap`, `@napplet/shim`, `nostr-tools` (required by kehto and applesauce; never imported) |

## Shared rules

- ESM only, TypeScript strict, `verbatimModuleSyntax`. Each package ships `dist/index.js` and `dist/index.d.ts` with `sideEffects: false`.
- Every public export has JSDoc with `@param`, `@returns` and `@example`, and appears in the [API reference](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/reference/api.md).
- Streams in `@kernl/core` are rxjs `Observable`s (`session$`, `guard.events$`, `grants.changes$`, `relays.changes$`, `AppletHandle.status$`); unsubscribe the `Subscription` they return. `MessagingBackend.subscribe` returns `{ subscriptionId }`, which you pass to `unsubscribe`. Thrown errors carry a stable prefixed reason: `denied:`, `invalid:`, `unavailable:`; the full list is in [Error reasons](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/reference/errors.md).
- No published package imports `nostr-tools` directly, and no published package depends on a UI framework. `pnpm check:deps` enforces both.
- Behaviour is specified in Gherkin under each package's `features/` and run by vitest with 100% coverage over `src`.

## Versioning

All packages are `0.x`. A breaking change is a `minor` bump; everything else is a `patch`. Releases are managed with changesets: one changeset per package whose shipped output changed. `@kernl/core` depends on the other three with `workspace:^`, so a release of a leaf package produces a patch of core.

## Install

The `@kernl/*` packages are not yet published to npm; `pnpm add @kernl/core` fails with a not-found error. During the alpha the source repository is private, and the packages are used from a clone of it:

```bash
# in a clone of the kernl source repository
pnpm install && pnpm build
```

`pnpm build` writes each package's `dist/`, which is what `main`, `types` and `exports` point at. Then add your code as a workspace package (under `packages/` or `apps/`, the globs in `pnpm-workspace.yaml`) and depend on what you need with the workspace protocol, as `apps/web` does:

```json
{
  "dependencies": {
    "@kernl/core": "workspace:^",
    "@kernl/guard": "workspace:^"
  }
}
```

Run `pnpm install` again after editing the manifest so pnpm links the workspace packages. `@kernl/core` pulls the other three in. Install a leaf package alone when you want its contract without kehto and applesauce, for example `@kernl/guard` to test an applet against the limits, or `@kernl/messaging` to write a provider.

---

<!-- https://kernlize.github.io/docs/packages/messaging.md -->

# @kernl/messaging

Messaging provider contract, registry, composite direct-message backend and an in-memory backend for the kernl shell. Pure: no relay code, no signer, no kehto dependency. Providers receive their backend constructor from the shell.

> **Network backends live in `@kernl/core`**
>
> This package ships no backend that sends anything over a network; the only backend in it is `createMemoryBackend`. The network backends for `private` and `legacy` are `createPrivateMessagesBackend` and `createLegacyMessagesBackend` in [`@kernl/core`](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/packages/core.md#messaging-backends), because they need the shell's event store, connection pool and account signer. `createKernl` wires them by default, so both providers work in the live shell while the signed-in account's signer can encrypt; `ratchet` stays unavailable with `no-runtime` ([Alpha status](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/alpha-status.md#messaging-providers-in-the-live-shell)). The offline preview (`?preview=1`) runs the same providers over the in-memory backend with a scripted correspondent, so messages sent there go nowhere.

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Package | `@kernl/messaging` |
| Version | `0.1.0` |
| Entry | `./dist/index.js`, types `./dist/index.d.ts` |
| Dependencies | none |
| Peer dependencies | `@napplet/core >=0.37.0 <0.38.0` (the `Dm*` wire types) |
| Side effects | none |

## Install

`@kernl/messaging` is not yet published to npm, so `pnpm add @kernl/messaging` fails. During the alpha it is built from the kernl source repository, which is private, and consumed as a workspace dependency. The [package index](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/packages/index.md#install) has the steps.

```json
{ "dependencies": { "@kernl/messaging": "workspace:^" } }
```

## Purpose

One contract for every private-messaging protocol, truthful self-description instead of ranking, and one composite backend that projects every enabled provider onto the NAP `dm` domain. The concepts are in [Messaging](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/concepts/messaging.md); the opinion is [D-009](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/decisions.md#d-009).

## Exports

### Contract

| Export | Signature | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `MessagingProvider` | interface | `{ id; name; description; properties: SecurityProperties; availability(): ProviderAvailability; createBackend(): MessagingBackend }`. `id` is the conversation-id prefix. |
| `MessagingBackend` | interface | `status()`, `conversations(query?)`, `messages(query)`, `send(request)`, `subscribe(request, onMessage)`, `unsubscribe(subscriptionId)`, `close?()`. Every method except `send` may return synchronously or a promise. Structurally kehto's `DmAdapter`. |
| `SecurityProperties` | interface | `forwardSecrecy`, `postCompromiseSecurity`, `metadataProtection: 'none' \| 'partial' \| 'strong'`, `requiresSameClient`, `groups`, `specification?`, `experimental`. |
| `ProviderAvailability` | union | `{ available: true }` or `{ available: false; reason: string }`. The reason is a bare word such as `sign-in-required`; the registry prefixes it as `unavailable:<reason>`. |
| `ProviderEntry` | interface | `{ provider; enabled: boolean; availability: ProviderAvailability }`, what `MessagingRegistry.list()` and `get()` return. |
| `MessagingPreferences` | interface | `{ enabled: readonly string[]; defaultProvider?: string }`, the persisted registry state. |
| `PACKAGE_NAME` | `'@kernl/messaging'` | The package name as a constant. |

### Registry

| Export | Signature | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `createMessagingRegistry` | `(options?: MessagingRegistryOptions) => MessagingRegistry` | One per shell. Owns one backend per enabled provider, restores saved preferences lazily as providers register, and hands out one stable composite backend. |
| `MessagingRegistryOptions` | interface | `{ preferences?: MessagingPreferences; onChange?: (preferences: MessagingPreferences) => void }`. `onChange` receives a frozen snapshot after every change. |
| `MessagingRegistry` | interface | `register(provider)`, `list()`, `get(id)`, `enable(id)`, `disable(id)`, `setDefault(id)`, `preferences()`, `composite()`, `close()`. Error reasons: `invalid:duplicate-provider`, `invalid:unknown-provider`, `unavailable:<reason>`, `invalid:provider-not-enabled`. |

### Composite backend

| Export | Signature | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `createCompositeBackend` | `(resolveEnabled: () => readonly EnabledBackend[], getDefault: () => string \| undefined) => MessagingBackend` | One backend over every enabled provider. Ids leaving it are `<providerId>:<innerId>`; ids arriving are routed by prefix. Rules for cursors, sends and subscriptions are in [Messaging](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/concepts/messaging.md#the-composite-backend). |
| `EnabledBackend` | interface | `{ id: string; backend: MessagingBackend }`. |
| `WithProvider<T>` | type | `T & { provider?: string }`: a `DmSendRequest` that names the provider for a new conversation. |
| `namespaceId` | `(providerId: string, innerId: string) => string` | `'private:direct:ab,cd'`. |
| `splitId` | `(id: string) => NamespacedId \| undefined` | Splits on the first `:`; `undefined` when there is no prefix. |
| `NamespacedId` | interface | `{ providerId: string; innerId: string }`. |

### In-memory backend

| Export | Signature | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `createMemoryBackend` | `(options?: MemoryBackendOptions) => MemoryBackend` | A complete backend in memory for tests and the shell's offline preview. Conversations are keyed `direct:<pubkey>` or `group:<pubkey>,<pubkey>` over the sorted correspondents; cursors are numeric offsets; unread is the count of `received` messages. |
| `MemoryBackendOptions` | interface | `{ owner?: string (default 'owner'); available?: boolean (default true); now?: () => number }`. `now` is in Unix seconds and defaults to the wall clock. |
| `MemoryBackend` | interface | `MessagingBackend` plus `deliver(incoming: MemoryIncoming): DmMessage` (stores a `received` message and notifies matching subscribers) and a non-optional `close()` that drops every subscriber. |
| `MemoryIncoming` | interface | `{ senderPubkey; content; conversationId?; createdAt? }`. Without `conversationId` the message lands in `direct:<senderPubkey>`. |

`send()` rejects with `invalid:no-recipients` when neither a conversation nor a recipient other than the owner is named, `invalid:unknown-conversation` for an id the backend has never seen, and `unavailable:offline` while `available` is false. Reads keep working offline.

### Providers

| Export | Signature | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `createPrivateMessagesProvider` | `(deps: ProviderDeps) => MessagingProvider` | Id `private`, name "Private messages". NIP-17. |
| `createLegacyMessagesProvider` | `(deps: ProviderDeps) => MessagingProvider` | Id `legacy`, name "Legacy messages". NIP-04. |
| `createRatchetMessagesProvider` | `(deps: ProviderDeps) => MessagingProvider` | Id `ratchet`, name "Ratchet sessions". nostr-double-ratchet draft; `experimental: true`. |
| `defineProvider` | `(definition: ProviderDefinition, deps: ProviderDeps) => MessagingProvider` | Joins fixed copy and properties with the shell's backend constructor and availability check. The three built-ins are made with it. |
| `ProviderDeps` | interface | `{ createBackend: () => MessagingBackend; available: () => ProviderAvailability }`. |
| `ProviderDefinition` | interface | `{ id; name; description; properties: SecurityProperties }`. |
| `describeProvider` | `(provider: MessagingProvider) => readonly ProviderDescriptionRow[]` | Six label/value rows for the picker, in a fixed order; `specification` is left out so no protocol name reaches the UI. |
| `ProviderDescriptionRow` | interface | `{ label: string; value: string }`. |

## Example

```ts
import { createCompositeBackend, createMemoryBackend, createMessagingRegistry, createPrivateMessagesProvider } from '@kernl/messaging';

const backend = createMemoryBackend({ owner: 'me', now: () => 1_700_000_000 });
await backend.send({ recipients: ['alice'], content: 'hi' });
backend.deliver({ senderPubkey: 'alice', content: 'hello' });

const registry = createMessagingRegistry({ onChange: (prefs) => console.log(prefs) });
registry.register(createPrivateMessagesProvider({ createBackend: () => backend, available: () => ({ available: true }) }));
registry.enable('private');
registry.setDefault('private');

const page = await registry.composite().conversations({ limit: 20 });
page.conversations[0]?.id; // 'private:direct:alice'

// the same composite, assembled by hand
createCompositeBackend(() => [{ id: 'private', backend }], () => 'private');
```

## Scope

- Holds no relay, store or signer. The shell passes a `createBackend` function; what it closes over is the shell's business.
- Does not rank, score or recommend. `SecurityProperties` is rendered verbatim by `describeProvider`.
- Does not translate wire types; `@napplet/core`'s `Dm*` types are used directly.
- Owns backend lifetimes through the registry. The composite's `close()` is a no-op by design.

## Specification

`packages/messaging/features/`: `registry.feature`, `composite.feature`, `memory-backend.feature`, `providers.feature`.

## API reference

Generated module: [`_kernl_messaging`](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/api/modules/_kernl_messaging.html)

# Policies

Rules the repository enforces mechanically. Each policy names the script that checks it and the decision in `DECISIONS.md` that motivates it. A policy that cannot be checked by a script is a convention, and conventions live in `AGENTS.md`, not here.

| Policy | Checked by | Decision |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Public vocabulary](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/policies/public-vocabulary.md) | `pnpm check:vocabulary` (`scripts/check-public-vocabulary.mjs`) | [D-006](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/decisions.md#d-006) |
| [Security posture](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/policies/security-posture.md) | `packages/*/features/` scenarios, `pnpm check:deps`, Playwright in `pnpm test:e2e` | [D-001](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/decisions.md#d-001), [D-002](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/decisions.md#d-002), [D-003](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/decisions.md#d-003) |
| [Spec conformance](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/policies/spec-conformance.md) | `packages/*/features/` scenarios; review. Running `@napplet/conformance` in the suite is [roadmap](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/roadmap.md#_7-conformance) work. | `AGENTS.md` "Spec before code" |

Two further gates apply to everything, including these pages:

- **Docs gate.** `pnpm docs:check` builds TypeDoc and VitePress, then runs `scripts/audit-docs.mjs`: a page per package with its version row, every page in the sidebar, a TypeDoc module per package, `llms.txt`, `llms-full.txt` and a Markdown twin per built page.
- **Slop gate.** `pnpm slop` runs aislop over the repository and `scripts/assert-slop-score.mjs` fails below 100. Functions under 120 lines, files under 600, nesting under 4, at most 5 parameters, no narrative comments.

<!-- https://kernlize.github.io/docs/policies/public-vocabulary.md -->

# Public vocabulary

The public website and the shell UI never name a protocol. The person is the point; the protocol is plumbing. This page is the denylist, the reasoning, and where the rule stops.

## The rule

`scripts/check-public-vocabulary.mjs` scans the built output of `apps/web` (the landing pages and the shell's UI copy) and fails the build on any of these, case-insensitively, as whole words or prefixes where marked:

| Denied | Say instead |
| --- | --- |
| `nostr` | "your account", "the network" |
| `nip-` (prefix) | describe the behaviour: "signing extension", "remote signer", "private messages" |
| `napplet` | "applet" |
| `relay` | "network", or nothing: the user's relays are "where your account lives" |
| `pubkey` | "account", "address" |
| `npub` | "address" |
| `nsec` | "secret key", in the one place the shell must warn about it |

Two checks enforce it:

- **Build time.** `scripts/check-public-vocabulary.mjs` reads every HTML, Markdown, text, JSON and XML file in the Pages artifact outside `docs/`, so Astro pages, JSON-LD, `llms.txt` and the Markdown twins are covered.
- **In a browser.** `tests/e2e/public-vocabulary.spec.ts` loads every public page and walks the shell (sign-in, launcher, applet summary, a running applet's frame, the consent dialog with its record view open, and the guard, messages, grants and settings panels). It reads what a person can perceive: rendered text, `title`, `aria-label`, `placeholder` and `alt`. Copy rendered by scripts, which the file scan cannot see, is covered here.

Identifiers inside JavaScript bundles are not copy and are not checked. The consent dialog's record view shows every field of the event it will sign, with plain labels ("Signed by", "Type", "Labels") instead of wire field names.

## Why

Three reasons, in the order `SOUL.md` ranks them.

**The user's agency.** A person deciding whether to run an applet needs to know what it will do and what it can reach. A protocol name tells them nothing about either; it tells them which club they are supposed to already belong to. "This applet wants to publish on your behalf" is a decision a person can make. "This applet requires `relay` and `outbox`" is not.

**Protocol conformance is a property of the code, not the copy.** kernl conforms to NIP-5D and the NAPs, and the docs say so precisely. Saying so on the landing page would not make the code conform more; it would make the page about the specification instead of about what a person can do.

**Providers and bridges are chosen by what they do.** A user chooses a messaging provider by whether their correspondent can read it and what an observer learns, not by its wire format. A bridge is "downloads", not the name of a peer-to-peer protocol. Naming protocols in the UI would invite ranking by familiarity, which [D-009](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/decisions.md#d-009) and [D-010](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/decisions.md#d-010) rule out.

## Where the rule stops

- **These docs.** Written for developers, who need the names. Every page here uses them.
- **Code, specs, commit messages, issues.** `napplet` is the protocol term and stays in identifiers and in `features/`.
- **`specification` fields.** `SecurityProperties.specification` and a bridge's protocol are shown in the docs, never in the picker.
- **Addresses.** Server URLs a user adds, edits or removes are data, and their hostnames belong to whoever runs the server. Both checks ignore `http(s)://` and `ws(s)://` URLs.
- **The secret-key warning.** The one place the shell mentions `nsec` is the warning that it will never ask for one.

## The words we use

| Say | Not | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| applet | napplet, app, dapp | "napplet" remains the protocol term in code and specs. |
| shell | OS, desktop, browser | kernl runs in a browser; it is not one. |
| grant | permission, capability | A grant is something the user gave and can take back. |
| provider | protocol | Users choose providers by what they do. |
| guard | firewall, mitigation | The guard is the set of protections between an applet and the user. |

Marketing adjectives, filler and hedges that hide a decision are out everywhere, including here.

---

<!-- https://kernlize.github.io/docs/policies/security-posture.md -->

# Security posture

The rules the shell keeps when it runs untrusted code next to the user's identity. Each rule has a scenario in `packages/*/features/` or a check in `scripts/`; a rule with neither is a wish.

## Mount rules

1. **`srcdoc`, never `src`.** The applet document is the verified bytes with the shell prelude and CSP injected outside the signed content. A `src` URL would give the applet an origin and a network path the shell does not mediate.
2. **`sandbox="allow-scripts"` only.** `mountApplet` sets the attribute to exactly `allow-scripts`, replacing any tokens the host set. Never `allow-same-origin`, never `allow-top-navigation`, never `allow-popups`. The frame has an opaque origin and cannot reach the shell's storage or DOM.
3. **The guard's CSP, unchanged by profile.** `createAppletCsp(profile)` is applied through `prepareNappletSrcdoc`, and `planMount` appends its `trustedTypes` directives (`require-trusted-types-for 'script'; trusted-types default`) to the CSP meta kehto rendered; it returns the same policy for every profile. No grant, profile or setting alters it. See [Guard](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/concepts/guard.md#why-csp-never-loosens).
4. **No controllers.** On the attached, still empty frame, before any applet document exists, `mountApplet` calls kehto's `denyNappletControllerAccess(frame)`, which rewrites the frame's `allow` attribute (its Permissions Policy) to end in `gamepad 'none'; hid 'none'; usb 'none'` and drops any entry the host had set for those three features. A frame without `getAttribute` gets the same value as `CONTROLLER_DENY_POLICY`. This rule is about game controllers and USB or HID devices only. Workers, service workers included, are refused by the CSP's `worker-src 'none'` (rule 3), not by this policy.
5. **Order: attached empty frame → harden → register → set environment → observe frame → assign `srcdoc`.** The host attaches the iframe to the document first, with no `src` or `srcdoc` (`mountApplet` throws `invalid:frame-detached` without a `contentWindow`). Then `mountApplet` sets `sandbox` and the controller policy, `originRegistry.register(contentWindow, windowId, identity)`, then `originRegistry.setEnvironment(contentWindow, environment)`, then `bridge.observeFrame(frame, windowId)`, then `frame.srcdoc = plan.srcdoc`. Assigning `srcdoc` first would let the document's first message arrive before the shell knows who it is.
6. **The host page forbids frame navigation.** The HTML the server sends carries `KERNL_FRAME_POLICY_META`, kehto's `<meta http-equiv="Content-Security-Policy" content="frame-src 'none'">`, in its `<head>` before any script runs, as `apps/web/src/pages/app/index.astro` does. Applet frames still load, because their bytes arrive as `srcdoc`; a frame that tries to load or navigate to a URL is blocked, so an applet cannot replace its verified document before kehto sees its first load. kehto warns in the console when the policy is missing. See [Embed kernl core](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/how-tos/embed-kernl-core.md).
7. **Remove the iframe on every revocation reason.** `window-message`, `second-hello`, `invalid-hello`, `second-load`, `port-closed` and `host` all end with the frame gone and the guard's state for the window forgotten. A revoked window's identity is never re-bound to the same frame.
8. **No frame in the applet's markup.** `planMount` calls `assertAppletHasNoFrame` on the verified bytes before they become a `srcdoc`, and refuses markup containing an `iframe`, `frame`, `frameset`, `object`, `embed`, `portal` or `fencedframe` element with `denied:nested-frame`. It parses with the host's `DOMParser` when there is one and otherwise matches lexically, which may over-reject ([D-014](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/decisions.md#d-014)).
9. **The frame lock runs before applet code.** `planMount` inserts `renderFrameLockScript()` immediately after kehto's namespace prelude. It installs the Trusted Types `default` policy, which refuses frame markup at every HTML string sink, and pins `createElement`, `createElementNS` and `createDocument` so they throw `denied:nested-frame` for a frame tag. Because frames can also be minted without a factory, the same script pins every DOM insertion method to refuse a node that is or contains a frame element, refuses custom elements that extend frames, and removes `XSLTProcessor`; a frame never becomes connected, so it never gets a realm. When kehto's prepared head is not where `planMount` expects it, the mount is refused with `unavailable:frame-lock` rather than run without the lock. This is a port of kehto's unreleased `nestedContextLock`, removed when `@kehto/shell` ships it ([D-014](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/decisions.md#d-014)).

## Identity rules

10. **Verified bytes come from `@kehto/nip/5d` `resolveNapplet`.** Gateways and caches are accelerators; the hash is the identity. Cached bytes are re-verified on every read.
11. **Identity is `(dTag, artifactHash)` plus one port.** Grants are keyed by that identity; a new build is a new identity with no grants.
12. **Restrictive by narrowing.** `resolveEnvironment` returns only granted domains; kehto intersects, so the hook can only remove. The runtime's permissive default is never reached for an ungranted domain.

## Key rules

13. **Keys live only inside applesauce signer instances.** `ExtensionSigner`, `NostrConnectSigner`, `PasswordAccount`'s wrapped signer. kernl never holds raw key bytes and never serialises a private key outside `PasswordAccount`.
14. **The shell never gives an applet `window.nostr`.** kehto's prelude installs `window.napplet` and nothing that signs; the shell does not forward the page's signer, and every signature an applet gets goes through rule 15. kernl does not control browser extensions: one that injects scripts into every frame can still reach into an applet's frame and expose its own signing object there, which no rule on this page governs. The guarantee is about what the shell provides, not about what the user's extensions add.
15. **Destructive signatures wait for the user.** An applet can ask for a signature only through a granted domain. When an applet window asks the shell to sign a destructive kind (every replaceable kind: 0, 3 and 10000–19999; every addressable kind, 30000–39999; a deletion, kind 5; a request to vanish, kind 62), `@kernl/core`'s consent gate looks up the version it replaces, in the event store and then over the outbox and discovery relays for up to `CURRENT_VERSION_TIMEOUT_MS` (4 s), shows the change as a semantic diff through `host.presentConsent` and waits. When no current version is found, the summary says so first ("Current version: could not be loaded; this replaces it entirely") rather than reading as a harmless first version; a denial fails with `denied:consent` and nothing is signed or published. Both routes pass the gate: `relay.publish` through the signer kernl returns from `ShellAdapter.auth.getSigner(windowId)`, and `outbox.publish` in kernl's outbox service wrapper, because kehto's outbox service signs without naming the window. The shell's own signing, with no window, is not gated. Routine kinds are signed without a prompt, and answers are not remembered. kehto's runtime has no such step; this rule is kernl's.

## Network rules

16. **No applet network path exists outside the shell.** All bytes arrive through the `resource` domain and a bridge. An applet frame has no network of its own, and cannot make a child frame that would have one: kehto's prelude pins every `RTC*` global (and the `webkit`/`moz` variants) to `undefined`, read-only and non-configurable; rules 8 and 9 stop the applet from creating a child realm where those globals still work; and the CSP refuses `fetch`, WebSocket, images, frame loads and beacons. `tests/e2e/applet-network-sealed.spec.ts` proves this in a real browser: 15 frame-creation routes throw, no child realm and no peer-connection constructor exists, and no `srflx` or `relay` candidate is gathered. When the host page can reach a public STUN server, the spec asserts that it does and that the applet produces no such candidate; otherwise that control is skipped. The HTTP bridge enforces `https` only, 10 MiB, 20 s and a private-address block over IPv4 and fully parsed IPv6 literals ([Bridges](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/concepts/bridges.md#the-http-bridge)). In Node and on servers it follows up to 3 redirects by hand and re-checks every hop; in a browser a redirect is opaque to it and is refused with `denied:redirect-unverifiable`. Hostnames are checked as literals only: no resolver is wired, so a public name that resolves to a private address is not caught. Browser fetches are also subject to CORS: a request the browser blocks is `unavailable:network Failed to fetch`, and any other status-0 answer is `unavailable:network <type> response`.
17. **One `RelayPool`.** No service, provider or bridge opens its own connection. Adapters over the shared pool satisfy kehto's contracts.
18. **Hidden windows are watched, not paused.** The visibility gate holds only a hidden window's window-level `hello`. Port traffic is observed just before kehto dispatches it, and the observation cannot hold it ([D-012](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/decisions.md#d-012)): a hidden window's activity is recorded and its overruns of the unfocused budget are reported, while its `resource.*` request past the hidden allowance quarantines it, and that request is not dispatched.

## Log rules

19. **Secrets never appear in logs, guard events or consent summaries.** `GuardEvent.reason` is a stable prefixed string; `NappletRevocation.detail` never includes message payloads; `describeChange` output names fields, not key material.
20. **Guard events are shown to the user**, with the applet and the reason. They are not sent anywhere.

## Dependency rules

21. **`nostr-tools` is never imported by kernl source.** It is a direct peer dependency of `@kernl/core`, because kehto and applesauce require it, but no file under `packages/*/src` imports it.
22. **Published packages have zero framework dependencies.** `svelte`, `react`, `vue`, `preact`, `solid-js` and `lit` are forbidden in every `packages/*/package.json`.
23. **Leaf packages do not import `@kehto/*`**, except `@kernl/guard`, which imports `@kehto/firewall`. Only `@kernl/core` composes kehto.

Rules 21 to 23 are enforced by `scripts/check-dependency-rules.mjs` (`pnpm check:deps`). Rules 1 to 20 are scenarios in `packages/*/features/` (the root `features/support/` only wires their step definitions into vitest), and the mount rules are additionally exercised in the browser by the Playwright suite.

## Reporting

A posture violation is a bug of the highest severity in this repository, above any feature. Report it to the maintainers with the rule number; the source repository is private during the alpha. If it involves a kehto seam, the issue is filed upstream too, and `DECISIONS.md` records the gap.

---

<!-- https://kernlize.github.io/docs/policies/spec-conformance.md -->

# Spec conformance

kernl conforms to specifications it does not own. This page says which ones, what "upstream first" means in practice, and how a gap is recorded.

## Authority

| Area | Authority | Local copy |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Shell–applet protocol | NIP-5D, [nostr-protocol/nips PR #2303](https://github.com/nostr-protocol/nips/pull/2303) | none |
| NAP domains (`relay`, `outbox`, `dm`, `resource`, …) | [napplet/naps](https://github.com/napplet/naps) | none |
| Wire types and dispatch | [`@napplet/core`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@napplet/core), pinned `>=0.37.0 <0.38.0` | the installed package |
| Shell composition | kehto source, `@kehto/*` at the pinned ranges | the installed packages |
| Event layer | applesauce v7, [applesauce.build](https://applesauce.build) | the installed packages |
| Messaging protocols | NIP-17, NIP-04, the nostr double-ratchet draft, as named in each provider's `specification` | none |

kernl keeps no local copy of a specification text. A copy drifts; a link does not. When the PR or a NAP document changes, the behaviour changes in kernl in a pull request that cites the clause.

## Upstream first

When kernl needs something a specification or an upstream package does not provide, the order is:

1. **Compose it from what exists.** Most of kernl is this: the guard composes `@kehto/firewall`'s `evaluate()`, the restrictive posture composes `resolveEnvironment` and `aclState.grant`.
2. **Propose it upstream.** An issue or pull request on `kehto/web`, `napplet/naps` or `nostr-protocol/nips`, as appropriate. The four kehto gaps kernl has found, filed upstream as kehto/web #397–#400, are listed in [Alpha status](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/alpha-status.md#upstream-gaps).
3. **Implement it locally with a recorded gap.** Only when 1 is impossible and 2 is pending. The local implementation sits behind an interface, cites the upstream issue, and is removed when upstream lands.

kernl never re-implements a kehto primitive because it was easier than reading kehto's source, and never invents wire format. When a NAP is ambiguous, kernl prefers an upstream issue over a guess and records the ambiguity next to the code.

## What conformance is checked by

- **Gherkin scenarios** in `packages/*/features/` for every protocol-visible behaviour, named after the clause they implement where one exists.
- **Review.** A change that touches an envelope shape, a domain's semantics or the handshake cites the clause in its description. A reviewer checks the clause, not the summary.

`@napplet/conformance` (envelope validators per NAP domain, manifest validation and the reference mock shell's expectations of a host) is not part of the test suite yet; running it against the shell's bridge is on the [Roadmap](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/roadmap.md#_7-conformance).

The docs are non-normative. Where a page here and the specification disagree, the specification wins and the page has a bug.

## Recording a gap

A gap is anything kernl does that the specification does not say, or does not do that the specification says. Record it in three places:

1. **Next to the code**, as a comment that names the clause and the upstream issue. This is one of the few comments the slop gate accepts, because a reader could not infer it.
2. **In `DECISIONS.md`**, as a `D-NNN` entry with Context, Decision, Consequences and Reversal cost. If the gap is a kehto seam, the entry says what upstream change would close it.
3. **In [Alpha status](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/alpha-status.md)**, under upstream gaps, so a reader deciding whether to depend on kernl sees it without reading the decisions log.

A gap closes when upstream lands and the local layer is deleted. The `DECISIONS.md` entry stays, with a `Superseded by` line.

## Tie-breaking

Protocol conformance is second in `SOUL.md`'s tie-breakers, below the user's safety and agency and above the applet developer's ability to build. A conformance requirement that would weaken the user's position is not implemented silently; it is raised upstream with the conflict stated, and `DECISIONS.md` records which way kernl went while the question is open.

---

<!-- https://kernlize.github.io/docs/reference/api.md -->

# API reference

The API reference is generated from source JSDoc by TypeDoc 0.28 with `entryPointStrategy: packages` over the four workspaces in `typedoc.json`. It is written to `docs/api/` and served next to this site at `/docs/api/`.

```bash
pnpm docs:api
```

Do not edit the generated files. Fix the JSDoc in `packages/*/src` and rerun. `treatWarningsAsErrors` is on, so an export without documentation or a broken `{@link}` fails the build. The reference has no source links: `typedoc.json` sets `packageOptions.disableSources: true`, because the source repository is private during the alpha. Read the source in a clone instead.

## Modules

| Package | Module page |
| --- | --- |
| `@kernl/guard` | [`_kernl_guard`](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/api/modules/_kernl_guard.html) |
| `@kernl/messaging` | [`_kernl_messaging`](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/api/modules/_kernl_messaging.html) |
| `@kernl/bridges` | [`_kernl_bridges`](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/api/modules/_kernl_bridges.html) |
| `@kernl/core` | [`_kernl_core`](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/api/modules/_kernl_core.html) |

The [index page](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/api/index.html) lists all four, and the [hierarchy page](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/api/hierarchy.html) shows type relationships across them.

## How to read it

- Each module page lists its exports by kind: interfaces, type aliases, functions, variables. Every entry has at least one `@example`.
- Reasons in thrown errors are documented as string literals (`denied:…`, `invalid:…`, `unavailable:…`) on the function that throws them.
- Types imported from `@kehto/*` or `@napplet/core` are linked to their names but not expanded; `excludeExternals` keeps the reference to kernl's own surface.
- The reference is HTML only. It has no Markdown twin and is not included in `llms-full.txt`; the [package pages](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/packages/index.md) carry the export lists in Markdown for agents.

## Audit

`scripts/audit-docs.mjs` asserts that `docs/api/modules/_kernl_<package>.html` exists for every `packages/*/package.json`, that each package page links to it, and that the built docs carry their Markdown twins. It also reads every built page and checks that each `href` into `api/` resolves, under `VITEPRESS_BASE` (default `/docs/`), to a file TypeDoc wrote; that is why the links on this page are relative (`../api/…`). It runs as part of `pnpm docs:check`.

# Error reasons

Every failure in the four packages carries a stable reason string with a prefix that says what kind of failure it is. Code matches on the string; the UI maps it to words. This page lists each reason the packages throw or report, collected from `packages/*/src`.

| Prefix | Means |
| --- | --- |
| `denied:` | A policy or the user said no. Retrying the same request will not help. |
| `invalid:` | The input is malformed or names something that does not exist. |
| `unavailable:` | Something needed is missing or unreachable right now: a backend, a server, a provider. |

Thrown reasons are the `message` of an `Error`. A few carry a detail after a space (`denied:scheme http:`), so match on the part before the first space.

## Thrown errors

| Reason | Package | Thrown by | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `invalid:pointer` | `@kernl/core` | `decodePointer` | The input is not an `naddr`, `nevent`, `note`, 64-hex event id or coordinate. |
| `unavailable:manifest` | `@kernl/core` | `fetchManifestEvent`, so `Kernl.resolve` | No relay in the hints or the `apps` tier returned the manifest event. |
| `unavailable:blob` | `@kernl/core` | `defaultFetchBlob`, `resolveApplet` | No server returned the artifact bytes. kehto's `blob-unavailable` maps here. |
| `invalid:invalid-signature`, `invalid:invalid-manifest`, `invalid:aggregate-mismatch`, `invalid:blob-hash-mismatch`, `invalid:missing-index` | `@kernl/core` | `resolveApplet` | Verification failed. The part after `invalid:` is kehto's `NappletResolutionErrorCode`. Nothing runs. |
| `invalid:unresolved` | `@kernl/core` | `Kernl.plan` | The summary was not produced by this shell's `resolve`, so no verified bytes are held for it. |
| `denied:blocked` | `@kernl/core` | `Kernl.plan` | The user blocked this applet identity. |
| `denied:nested-frame` | `@kernl/guard`, `@kernl/core` | `assertAppletHasNoFrame`, so `planMount` and `Kernl.plan`; in the applet's realm, the frame lock | The verified markup contains an `iframe`, `frame`, `frameset`, `object`, `embed`, `portal` or `fencedframe` element, so the applet is not mounted. Inside a running applet the frame lock throws it as a `TypeError` when applet code tries to create a frame by element factory or HTML string ([D-014](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/decisions.md#d-014)). |
| `unavailable:frame-lock` | `@kernl/core` | `planMount`, so `Kernl.plan` | The srcdoc kehto prepared does not contain the CSP meta and namespace prelude where kernl expects them, so the frame lock cannot be inserted and the applet is not mounted. Seen only with a kehto release whose output changed. |
| `invalid:frame-detached` | `@kernl/core` | `mountApplet`, so `Kernl.mount` | The frame has no `contentWindow`; it is not in the document. |
| `invalid:domain` | `@kernl/core` | `Grants.allowDomain` | The shell does not offer this domain in its current configuration. |
| `denied:baseline-domain` | `@kernl/core` | `Grants.revokeDomain` | Baseline domains (`shell`, `inc`, `theme`, `storage`) cannot be revoked. |
| `denied:plaintext-key-persistence` | `@kernl/core` | `KernlAccountManager.addAccount` | The account type stores a raw secret key (`PLAINTEXT_KEY_ACCOUNT_TYPES`). |
| `invalid:relay-url` | `@kernl/core` | `RelayTiers.add` | The URL is not `ws://` or `wss://`. |
| `denied:read-only` | `@kernl/core` | the outbox service's signer | The session cannot sign, so an outbox publish is refused. |
| `denied:consent` | `@kernl/core` | `createSigningConsent`, through the window signer (`relay.publish`) or the outbox gate (`outbox.publish`) | An applet window asked to sign a destructive kind (any replaceable or addressable kind, 5 or 62) and the user denied or dismissed `host.presentConsent`. Nothing was signed or published. |
| `denied:unknown-applet` | `@kernl/core` | `createSigningConsent` | A destructive write from a window the shell did not mount. |
| `denied:signed-out` | `@kernl/core` | `createSigningConsent` | A destructive write (in practice an `outbox.publish`) while nobody is signed in. |
| `invalid:event-kind` | `@kernl/core` | `createSigningConsent` | The event's `kind` is not a number. |
| `unavailable:sign-in-required` | `@kernl/core` | `createDefaultMessaging`'s `createBackend`; `MessagingRegistry.enable` | `private` or `legacy` while no account is active (`MESSAGING_UNAVAILABLE_REASONS`). |
| `unavailable:signer-cannot-encrypt` | `@kernl/core` | `createDefaultMessaging`'s `createBackend`; `MessagingRegistry.enable` | The active account's signer has no `nip44` (`private`) or no `nip04` (`legacy`); a read-only account is the usual case. |
| `unavailable:no-runtime` | `@kernl/core` | `createDefaultMessaging`'s `createBackend`; `MessagingRegistry.enable` | `ratchet`: no double-ratchet runtime is supplied. |
| `invalid:duplicate-provider` | `@kernl/messaging` | `MessagingRegistry.register` | A provider with this id is already registered. |
| `invalid:unknown-provider` | `@kernl/messaging` | `MessagingRegistry.enable`, `disable`; the composite backend | No provider has this id, or a namespaced id, cursor or `provider` hint names no enabled provider. |
| `unavailable:<reason>` | `@kernl/messaging` | `MessagingRegistry.enable` | The provider's `availability()` is false; `<reason>` is the bare word it reported. |
| `invalid:provider-not-enabled` | `@kernl/messaging` | `MessagingRegistry.setDefault` | Only an enabled provider can be the default. |
| `unavailable:no-default-provider` | `@kernl/messaging` | composite `send` | The request names no conversation and no provider, and there is no enabled default. |
| `invalid:no-recipients`, `invalid:unknown-conversation`, `unavailable:offline` | `@kernl/messaging` | `createMemoryBackend` `send` | No recipient besides the owner; a `conversationId` the backend does not hold; the backend was created with `available: false`. |
| `invalid:recipient`, `invalid:groups-unsupported`, `unavailable:offline` | `@kernl/core` | `createPrivateMessagesBackend`, `createLegacyMessagesBackend` `send` | The recipient is not a public key; the legacy backend got more than one correspondent; no relay accepted the message. |
| `invalid:locator` | `@kernl/bridges` | `parseLocator` | Not a locator, or a malformed web, NZB, Soulseek or mail locator. |
| `invalid:magnet-missing-hash` | `@kernl/bridges` | `parseLocator` | A magnet without a `urn:btih:` hash. |
| `invalid:locator-missing-<field>` | `@kernl/bridges` | the torrent, NZB, Soulseek and mail bridges | The locator lacks `infoHash`, `url`, `user`, `path` or `address`. |
| `invalid:nzb-not-https` | `@kernl/bridges` | the NZB backend from `createHandoffBackends` | The NZB document is not served over `https`, so it is not handed off and nothing is opened. |
| `invalid:duplicate-bridge <id>`, `invalid:scheme-taken <scheme>` | `@kernl/bridges` | `BridgeRegistry.register` | A bridge with this id, or one serving this scheme, is already registered. |
| `unavailable:no-bridge` | `@kernl/bridges` | `BridgeRegistry.resolve` | No bridge serves the scheme. |
| `unavailable:no-backend` | `@kernl/bridges` | the four backend-driven bridges | The bridge was created without a backend. `availability().reason` is the bare `no-backend`. In the composed shell the four have hand-off backends; a registry built from `createDefaultBridges()` without a `handoff` opener reports this. |
| `denied:bridge` | `@kernl/bridges` | `BridgeRegistry.resolve` | The registry's `authorize` hook returned false. The composed shell has none. |
| `denied:scheme <protocol>` | `@kernl/bridges` | HTTP bridge | The URL's scheme is not in `allowedSchemes`. |
| `denied:private-address <host>`, `denied:private-address <host> -> <ip>` | `@kernl/bridges` | HTTP bridge | The host is a blocked name or a private literal; the second form comes from a `resolveHost` result. |
| `denied:too-many-redirects` | `@kernl/bridges` | HTTP bridge | More than `maxRedirects` hops. |
| `denied:redirect-unverifiable` | `@kernl/bridges` | HTTP bridge | In a browser, `fetch` with `redirect: 'manual'` returns an opaque redirect whose target the bridge cannot read, so it cannot re-check the next hop and refuses. In Node and on servers redirects are followed and checked. |
| `invalid:redirect` | `@kernl/bridges` | HTTP bridge | A redirect without a usable `Location`. |
| `denied:too-large` | `@kernl/bridges` | HTTP bridge | `content-length` or the streamed body exceeds `maxBytes`. |
| `unavailable:timeout`, `unavailable:aborted`, `unavailable:network <message>` | `@kernl/bridges` | HTTP bridge | The time limit expired, the caller cancelled, or `fetch` failed for another reason. In a browser a CORS refusal and a network failure are the same `TypeError`, so both surface as `unavailable:network Failed to fetch`. |
| `unavailable:network <type> response` | `@kernl/bridges` | HTTP bridge | Any status-0 answer other than an opaque redirect, for example `unavailable:network opaque response`. |

Apart from `assertAppletHasNoFrame`, `@kernl/guard` throws nothing. Its decisions are events.

## Guard event reasons

The guard reports each non-pass decision as a `GuardEvent` with a `disposition` (`defer`, `reject`, `quarantine`, `flag`) and one of these reasons. They reach the user through `kernl.guard.events$` and the shell's guard panel. The numbers are per profile; see [Guard](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/concepts/guard.md#profiles).

For an applet's port traffic these layers observe each envelope just before kehto dispatches it but cannot hold it ([D-012](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/decisions.md#d-012)): an event records what happened. Two reasons change the outcome. `size:<class>` makes kehto's runtime firewall refuse that envelope (`refuseCurrentDispatch`), and `quarantine` revokes the binding, which also stops the envelope that crossed the limit. Otherwise `defer` and `reject` hold or drop only the window-level `hello`.

Refusals by kehto's runtime firewall (the per-class rates and the startup burst) are not guard events: kehto answers the applet with an error whose message starts `firewall:`, and `ShellAdapter` does not forward the runtime's firewall events to the host ([upstream gap 1](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/alpha-status.md#upstream-gaps)). The focus firewall's `rate:<class>` events count the same rates, so the user still sees an applet that runs out.

| Reason | Emitted by | Disposition | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `flood:burst` | ingress guard (`ingress-guard.ts`) | `defer` | More messages in one second than `ingressBurst` allows. A `hello` is held; for port traffic this is a report. |
| `flood:queue-full` | ingress guard | `reject` | More than `ingressQueue` messages over the burst. A `hello` is dropped; for port traffic this is a report. |
| `flood:quarantine` | ingress guard | `quarantine` | `quarantineThreshold` messages in a rolling 10 s, or any message from a window already quarantined. The binding is revoked. |
| `flood:hidden-resource` | ingress guard | `quarantine` | A hidden window made more `resource.*` requests than `hiddenResourceAllowance`. The binding is revoked. |
| `size:<class>` | ingress guard | `reject` | The envelope is over the size cap for `resource:bytes`, `relay:subscribe` or `outbox:subscribe`. In the composed shell the runtime firewall refuses it before dispatch, so the applet receives a `firewall:` error and nothing is fetched. |
| `defer:queue-full` | visibility gate (`visibility-gate.ts`) | `reject` | The hidden window's deferral queue is full. Only the window-level `hello` passes through the gate. |
| `rate:<class>` | focus firewall (`focus-firewall.ts`) | `reject`, or `flag` when the rate's action is `flag` | kehto's `rate:opclass`, `rate:global` or `rate:default` rule fired; the reason names the class, for example `rate:relay:publish`. |
| `matcher:<id>` | focus firewall | `reject` | A kehto content matcher fired; the rule id is passed through unchanged. The guard's own matchers are `size:resource:bytes`, `size:relay:subscribe` and `size:outbox:subscribe`, and in the composed shell they cannot fire: the ingress guard rejects the same envelopes with `size:<class>` first, and the focus firewall sees only what it passed. A caller that runs the focus firewall alone can see `matcher:size:<class>`. |
| `policy:deny` | focus firewall | `reject` | The applet's policy in the guard's own firewall configuration is `deny`. kernl sets no policy there, so this appears only if a caller set one. |
| `prompt:<ruleId>` | focus firewall | `reject` | kehto's engine asked for a prompt (for example `prompt:policy:ask`); the guard has no UI and treats it as a rejection. |

## Revocation reasons

`KernlHost.onRevoked(windowId, reason)` receives kehto's revocation reasons (`window-message`, `second-hello`, `invalid-hello`, `second-load`, `port-closed`, `host`) or `quarantine` when the guard quarantined the window. See [Architecture](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/concepts/architecture.md#the-mount-path).

## Related

- [API reference](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/reference/api.md): each function's JSDoc names the reasons it throws.
- [Troubleshooting](https://kernlize.github.io/docs/guides/troubleshooting.md)
